slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop overthinking a date
and just have a good time
Stop rehearsing conversations in your head. You can't script a real person. Go in with curiosity instead of lines, and the conversation will find its own way.
Stop reading meaning into every reply. A short text often just means she's busy. Waiting calmly instead of analysing every word keeps you relaxed and yourself.
Decide one simple goal for the evening: have fun. Not impress, not win, not get a second date. Just enjoy the company. Everything else gets easier from there.
Fill your head with better things. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and having fresh thoughts leaves less room for anxious ones before a date.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Fresh thoughts leave less room for anxious ones before a date.

slides.texte_overlay: Breathe slowly on the way there. Four seconds in, six out, a few times. It sounds simple, but it calms your body so your mind can follow before you arrive.
Notice the good moments while they happen. Her laugh, a great view, a good dish. Paying attention to the present is the opposite of overthinking it.
Let the evening end without a verdict. You don't need to know right away if it worked. Sleep on it, and send a kind message the next day if you enjoyed it.
